attrs.reasoning: JP HTML tutorials gloss form `action` in katakana (「属性: action (アクション) の解説」). Prose prefers 送信先/リクエスト先 but those explain the concept rather than name the identifier.
HTTPメソッド is universal. No native competitor.
A JP htmx tutorial uses the exact word for the exact attribute: 「hx-trigger属性は…トリガー（発動）するために使用されます」.
Same source: 「更新ターゲットの指定: hx-target属性」. 対象 is the native alternative but far more generic.

Weakest of the five. スワップ is a real IT loanword but no JP source uses it for DOM content replacement — both JP htmx articles reach for 置換/挿入方式 instead. Keep primary for parity with English; add 置換 as an accepted alias.

events.reasoning: Fully naturalized noun and suru-verb; every beginner tutorial titled 「クリックイベント」.
Matches tutorial prose word-for-word. Neutral noun.
Standard. Mild flag: its most common on-screen role is the submit-button label (送信ボタン), so a beginner may read it as 'send' rather than 'was submitted'. Inherent to the word, not a reason to change.
Tutorials distinguish input from change using exactly this noun. Pairs against 変更 as input pairs against change.
Only term JP UI writing uses. DROP the listed alternate 集中 — it means mental concentration, never UI focus, and would confuse a beginner.

DEFECT. ぼかし is the image-processing sense (Photoshop ぼかしフィルター / ガウスぼかし) with no focus meaning in Japanese at all — a dev reading fx-トリガー="ぼかし" would expect a visual effect. e-words defines フォーカスアウト as precisely this event and lists ブラー as its synonym. Retain ブラー and フォーカス解除 as alternates.
Universal JP term for initialization, used for exactly this timing. DROP the alternate イニット — essentially no currency.
Fully naturalized; no native alternative in use.

candidates.reasoning: Real but low-frequency — appears as a gloss in JP API references. Informal writing keeps the English identifier plus prose. Safe to publish; don't expect クリック-level recognition.
Same evidence strength as キーダウン; a JP JS reference titles an entry 「event.onkeyup - キーアップ時に発生するイベント」. Publishing keeps the pair symmetric.

押下 is genuine and semantically exact but heavy SIer spec-document register — documented as not understood outside the industry, a poor fit for beginners, and it has no usable partner for mouseup. マウスダウン is attested in the JP javascript.info translation and pairs with マウスアップ. Keep マウス押下 as an alternate.

FABRICATED. Exact-phrase search returns zero results in the event sense — every hit is 脱マウス content about working without a mouse. 解放 means freeing a resource (memory, locks), not releasing a button. Consistent with its upstream round-trip failure.
Strongest candidate — fully naturalized JP noun with its own glossary entries, used in beginner tutorials.
Attested as a defined term; less common alone but inherits recognizability from the pair.
Well attested despite upstream round-trip failure. リサイズ is an equally real, more compact alternate worth adding; サイズ変更 is more transparent for beginners.

candidates.proposed: 読み込み first, then ロード
candidates.reasoning: Both real but the ordering is backwards for primary-first: 読み込み dominates tutorial prose by a wide margin while ロード survives mainly inside onload discussion.

variantNote: Katakana-vs-native is not uniform, and that is the main structural finding. Single-concept interactions have naturalized katakana nouns usable as identifiers (クリック, スクロール, フォーカス, マウスオーバー); compound English event names have no established katakana form — informal sources keep the Latin identifier and explain in prose. Where a plain Japanese noun exists it beats katakana in real usage (読み込み over ロード, 置換 over スワップ). The katakana candidates are weakest exactly where they are compounds coined to mirror English morphology.
overall: Eight of thirteen shipped terms are solid; one is a genuine error and one candidate is fabricated. ぼかし for blur is the serious problem. マウス解放 for mouseup has zero attestation. Smaller: reorder the load pair to 読み込み-first, and drop the 集中 / イニット alternates. The imperative-vs-event worry mostly does not apply in Japanese since kanji suru-nouns are aspect-neutral.
